messages:
zara: Hi team, first week laptop trouble. Received the Ubuntu 22.04 ThinkPad, set up LUKS full-disk encryption during first-boot, but after the first auto-upgrade it drops to a dracut/initramfs prompt asking for a LUKS recovery key that I never got. FleetDM shows the device as "pending" and I can't SSH in. Who can help with recovery/enrollment?
onboard-bot: Welcome to Redwood, @zara! :tada: IT handles device crypto/recovery and eng-infra handles Fleet onboarding. Pinging them now.
it-support: Hey Zara, sorry about that. Quick triage: were any files copied from an old drive, and did you create a separate /home or LVM? Can you paste the output of these from the initramfs shell if possible: `lsblk -f`, `cat /proc/cmdline`, and `cryptsetup status <name>` (use the LUKS name it asks for). If you can't run them, DM and we'll schedule a remote session.
zara: I can paste what I see from initramfs: `lsblk -f` shows sda with one crypto_LUKS partition mapped to cryptroot, and rootfs pointing to /dev/mapper/cryptroot. `cryptsetup status cryptroot` says key is required and UUID matches the one in GRUB. I didn't migrate any old data, fresh device.
eng-infra: Fresh device and a post-upgrade initramfs prompt usually means the initramfs image didn't include the cryptsetup hooks or the kernel upgrade updated the initramfs without the correct keyscript. Two options: (1) if you can boot a live USB we can chroot and rebuild initramfs and reinstall grub, then confirm the crypttab and /etc/crypttab entries; (2) we can have you ship the device to office for tech-assisted revive. We prefer guiding you through a live-USB chroot first. Do you have an available USB and another machine to create the live image?
zara: I do have a spare USB and can create a live USB from my personal laptop. I'm in a different timezone but available in ~90 minutes.
it-support: Great. We'll schedule a 45min remote session to walk you through the chroot process. Quick note: if you try to brute-force the recovery prompt with wrong keys it may lock out or slow attempts. Please don't enter random passwords.
people-ops: Welcome @zara! If this delays your onboarding tasks, we can provision a temporary cloud devbox while you recover the laptop. DM us if you want that.
sec-ops: Security note: do not upload private keys or secrets to the live USB image; we'll not ask for any SSO credentials until the device is re-enrolled in Fleet/SSO. We'll monitor the session.
zara: Session scheduled. One thing I noticed earlier in GRUB menuedit was an extra `cryptdevice=UUID=...:cryptroot ro quiet splash` entry and a different `initrd=/boot/initrd.img-5.15.0-xx-generic` than the one the installer created.
eng-infra: That mismatch explains it: the running GRUB entry likely points to an older initrd that doesn't contain the right cryptsetup initramfs hooks. During the kernel upgrade `/boot` might have been updated but `update-initramfs` or `grub-mkconfig` wasn't run in the right sequence due to a diverging package script on that build. We'll rebuild with `mount /dev/mapper/cryptroot /mnt && for d in /dev /proc /sys; do mount --bind $d /mnt$d; done && chroot /mnt update-initramfs -u -k all && update-grub`. We'll walk you through those exact commands in the remote.
nit-support: Quick logistics: I'll open a TeamViewer/AnyDesk session during the slot so eng-infra can guide commands. Please have the live USB and a backup disk ready in case we need to rsync user data.
zara: Remote started. Followed chroot steps, update-initramfs ran and updated images. We reran update-grub and verified `/boot/grub/grub.cfg` points to the new initrd. Rebooting now.
eng-infra: Rebooting should drop you to GRUB and then prompt for the LUKS passphrase normally. If the prompt appears, use the password you set during initial encryption. After successful boot we'll confirm Fleet agent auto-start and complete enrollment.
zara: Rebooted and prompted for passphrase, entered it and system booted to login. FleetDM now shows the host as "enrolled" and assigned to the new-hires policy. SSH into the host works and I can push dotfiles.
it-support: Closing the loop 14 please follow the onboarding doc to run `sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade` and then verify `systemctl status fleet` and `journalctl -u fleet -b` to confirm no agent errors.
people-ops: Awesome, welcome aboard @zara! If you want the temporary cloud devbox cancelled now that you're up, say so and we'll close it.
zara: Cancel the cloud box please, I'm back on my laptop. Thanks so much everyone for the quick help and the walk-through. :party:
